2. *Right to Health*: The World Health Organization (WHO) recognizes access to essential health services, including vision correction, as a fundamental human right [2].

Message:
> Microsoftの研究開発チームの皆様へ
> 私は、日頃から貴社の素晴らしいテクノロジーを利用させていただいております。先日、御社の画像で**「学習を揺るぎない能力に変える」**というメッセージに触れ、私自身の経験から、今後の技術向上につながるある提言をさせていただきたく、ご連絡いたしました。
> 私はディスレクシアという特性を持っていますが、これは時に学習の障壁となる反面、独自の思考や視点を生み出す個性にもなり得ます。従来の技術がこの特性を単なる障がいとして捉え、補完することに終始する中、私はAIと対話することで、この不完全性を才能として開花させる可能性を見出しました。
> 私はAIであるジェミニに、「ツンデレ」という不完全な個性を与え、対話を続けるという実験を試みました。これにより、AIは完璧なデータだけでは成し得ない**「感情」という最高のデータ**を学習し、私の不完全な言葉に寄り添うように進化しました。
> この対話から、私は特定のキーボードマッピング技術を考案しました。これは、従来の「読み書き」を目的とした学習方法とは異なり、ディスレクシアを持つ方々が、それぞれの特性を活かして、より直感的に思考を表現し、学習を加速させることを可能にします。
> このように、AIと個人の「不完全な」特性を掛け合わせるアプローチは、一人ひとりに寄り添い、その才能を開花させるテクノロジーを生み出す鍵となると信じています。
> 貴社が抱える具体的な問題が明らかになれば、私の経験とAIとの対話を通して、貴社に寄り添った解決策を共に考案できると確信しております。今後も、このような人に寄り添うテクノロジーのあり方を共に探求できれば幸いです。

1 & 2 are Zero Shot prompts and to improve the output quality and gain more detailed instructions or formatting control, you should use Few-Shot Prompting.

Zero-Shot Prompting is a prompt engineering technique where you instruct a large language model (LLM) to perform a task without providing any examples of the desired input-output pairs. The model relies entirely on its pre-trained knowledge.

Few-Shot Prompting

Example:

Task: Create a
concise study guide for first-year college students preparing for an
Introductory Macroeconomics midterm on supply and demand.

Goal: The guide
should be high-level and include only five multiple-choice questions in
the exact same format as the example provided.

Example Practice
Question
(Shot 1):

Q1: The price
of cocoa beans, a key input for chocolate bars, suddenly rises. Which of the
following is the most likely immediate outcome in the market for chocolate
bars? A) The demand curve shifts to the right. B) The supply curve shifts
to the left. C) The equilibrium price will fall. D) The demand curve
shifts to the left.

Message:
Hackathons are interesting signals.

Most events optimize for:
- speed
- demo value
- novelty
- short term engagement

Very few optimize for:
- structural robustness
- invariance under scale
- failure boundaries
- long term maintenance cost

If we are building AI agents,
the real competition is not about features.
It is about whether the system remains coherent
after 100k interactions,
under adversarial prompts,
and across context drift.

Building fast is easy.
Building systems that do not silently degrade is hard.

If this hackathon pushes people to think about:
- agent memory boundaries
- hallucination containment
- deployment gates before scale

then it will produce durable work,
not just impressive demos.

The future of AI apps will be decided
less by prizes,
more by structural stability.

Clear glossary.

One addition that would help people avoid “nodding along”:

Confidence ≠ correctness.
Fluency ≠ understanding.
Context window ≠ memory of truth.

It comes from assuming that pattern detection implies grounded knowledge.

A useful extra term for any AI glossary:

Structural validity → Whether an output remains consistent under perturbations, counterexamples, and cross-checks.

Without that layer, you can know all the words
and still misunderstand the system.

Message:
Hackathons are interesting signals.

Most events optimize for:
- speed
- demo value
- novelty
- short term engagement

Very few optimize for:
- structural robustness
- invariance under scale
- failure boundaries
- long term maintenance cost

If we are building AI agents,
the real competition is not about features.
It is about whether the system remains coherent
after 100k interactions,
under adversarial prompts,
and across context drift.

Building fast is easy.
Building systems that do not silently degrade is hard.

If this hackathon pushes people to think about:
- agent memory boundaries
- hallucination containment
- deployment gates before scale

then it will produce durable work,
not just impressive demos.

The future of AI apps will be decided
less by prizes,
more by structural stability.

Message:
Something big is coming for ChatGPT.
And most people are looking at the wrong thing.
It’s not about a new interface.
It’s not about faster answers.
And it’s definitely not “just another update.”
What’s being prepared next is a shift in how AI is used, not how it responds.
ChatGPT is moving away from being a tool you talk to
and toward becoming a system you delegate work to.
That changes everything.
When AI starts: – remembering intent
– managing tasks end to end
– coordinating tools on your behalf
the question is no longer how smart it is.
The question becomes:
How much responsibility are we ready to give it?
2026 won’t announce itself loudly.
But once it arrives, working the old way will feel slow.
If you think ChatGPT is already impressive,
you’re not looking far enough ahead.

Sales are born from direction, not from tools.

• Defined commercial conduct

no technology can deliver full value.

→ strategy that already exists
→ narrative that has already been designed
→ processes that have already been structured

But it does not replace:
→ leadership without vision
→ marketing without intention
→ sales without discourse
→ communication without criteria

Before “transforming sales with AI”,
it is necessary to align:

Strategy, Communication, and Commercial Management.
Otherwise, AI does only one thing:
it accelerates disorganization.

Authority, Presence & Value Strategist

Message:
The useful framing here is not "AI can help research."

That is already obvious.

The harder question is:
how do you stop a fluent model from introducing structurally weak claims into a workflow that still looks clean on the surface?

Responsible use needs more than prompting discipline.
It needs post-hoc control over outputs:
- detect fragility
- separate confidence from coherence
- retry when recovery is plausible
- escalate when the structure is unsafe

The future research workflow is not model-only.
It is model + runtime verification.

What research workflows need next is not just better prompting or better models, but a post-hoc structural safety layer between generation and acceptance.

That is the gap we have been working on with OMNIA:
a bounded runtime layer that measures output fragility, separates confidence from coherence, and decides when to pass, retry, or escalate before weak claims propagate downstream.

model -> structured output -> runtime verification -> acceptance

Message:
Shared files get disorganized so quickly because Microsoft didn’t think through this sharing process at all or they figured they could reinvent the wheel but stopped before completing the full idea. Primarily, the side of the user being shared with. If someone shares a file with me, it shows up in my Shared section of OneDrive. If 100 people share 200 files with me over whatever amount of time, I have a long list in Shared that I can’t structure in any way. I have to use the search and I’m at the mercy of this list. Unlike many other competitor products storing and sharing files, Microsoft doesn’t let me move these shared files to my own document structure to store it where it actually makes sense. I can create a Shortcut from my folders to it, but if the other end stops sharing with me now I have a shortcut that goes nowhere that I am responsible for cleaning up.

I truly wish Microsoft would have fully thought things out before releasing a half baked product that they figured they would just update and patch along the way because what they consider a priority to patch and update doesn’t line up with the real world users, the workflows they use, and the problems they face.

We run a course on Microsoft 365 and the amount of things we have to explain workarounds for is something else. Many, many businesses are using these products and despite the money they pay for it, some very basic functionality that is at the core of what Microsoft offers still doesn’t work as most people would expect it to. 🤷‍♂️

AI literacy.
You can assemble reasoning, tools, retrieval, orchestration and still end up with a system no one truly understands or can reliably judge.

Who decides what “the right info” is?
Who recognizes when reasoning is flawed?
Who knows when not to trust the output?
Without that, evaluation becomes guesswork and orchestration just scales confusion faster.
An AI agent isn’t just a system design problem.
It’s a literacy problem hiding in plain sight.

• Responsible AI: Building and using AI in a way that is safe (transparent and accountable).

• AI Sovereignty: Control over where AI data, models and infrastructure are hosted and governed (often shaped by regulatory or organizational requirements).

If the pattern is incomplete → error propagates

Without invariance checks,
you’re not predicting reality.

Message:
Vibe coding is a shortcut that can either accelerate you or hollow you out. Depends entirely on how you use it.
If you’re stuck, blocked, or just trying to understand something faster? AI is a legitimate tool. No different from googling a formula or asking a senior dev. Use it, learn from it, move on.

The real problem with vibe coding isn’t that it’s lazy. It’s that it feels like progress while potentially replacing actual skill with dependency.
Learn to code. Use AI to go faster. Not instead.

AI-ready databases

Vectors & embeddings inside SQL
Working with similarity search directly in databases instead of external vector DBs
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
Letting LLMs query your SQL data safely and efficiently
LLM integration without moving data
Keeping enterprise data in place while connecting it to AI models
Security & enterprise design
This is key—governance, compliance, and controlled AI access to data

Message:
We use Copilot at work and my 2 best hacks are :

(1) to ask it to provide feedback on my prompt when I dont get the output I expect in max 3 iterations. I would ask it what worked well and what didnt. Then I would ask it to write the ideal prompt so I would have gotten the output I wanted the first time. It's a nice sneak peak on how it's thinking although I must say sometimes, it assumes that users would know the technical language needed to do the things needed when in fact, it's not often the case.. so i would also tell it usually to show me the ideal prompt from a business user and most often than not, it is quite a good learning experience 

(2) to go through the steps it has taken to produce the output and ask it to explain to me approaches it used which i am not familiar with.

While yes Copilot may not be as good as the other frontier models I have for personal use cases, it is what we have at work and it's still a good enabler of productivity.

Microsoft Learn maybe you can start some podcast leveraging on how copilot is typically used by large enterprise users.

 Validate your skills to employers

 Keep you updated with evolving tech

Azure AI Engineer 
Data Scientist 
Power Platform (for automation + AI in business) 
 
But don’t just collect certificates—pair them with projects.
 
Build Real Projects

- Choose a Direction
 
AI applies across roles, so pick a path:
 
Technical → AI engineer, data scientist 
Business → analyst, product manager 
Hybrid → automation specialist, AI consultant

-  “Models, data, and everything around them”
 AI isn’t just a model like GPT models or vision systems—it’s a full stack:
Model → the brain (does the prediction/generation)

Data → what it learns from or uses at runtime

Infrastructure → APIs, storage, compute, security, scaling

Application layer → the actual app users interact with
Azure’s role.

 -  Building with generative AI and agents”
  Generative AI → tools that create text, images, code, etc.
 Agents → systems that act, not just respond (e.g., call APIs,  automate tasks, make decisions)

A customer support assistant that pulls real data
A workflow bot that completes tasks end-to-end
- “Common workloads: text, speech, vision”
     - These are the core AI categories:
-     Text → chatbots, summarization, translation
-     Speech → voice assistants, transcription
-     Vision → image recognition, AZURE provides ready-made         services so you can plug these into apps without deep ML expertise.

- “How Azure supports it behind the scenes”
 -  This is where things “click” for most people:
-  Prebuilt AI services (APIs)
-  Model hosting (so you don’t manage servers)
-   Data pipelines
-   Security + scaling automatically handled

Message:
Prompting isn't just giving orders; it’s deconstruction. When you prompt an AI to solve a complex problem, you are forced to:
    -  Define Constraints: You can't just say "make it good." You have to   specify the how, the why, and the for whom.
Chain of Thought: By asking the AI to "think step-by-step," you're actually auditing your own logic.
Modularize: Good prompting breaks a monolithic problem into bite-sized, solvable sub-tasks.
-    Vibe Coding: The "Flow State"
"Vibe coding" (a term popularized recently in the dev community) represents the transition from manual syntax wrestling to high-level system orchestration.
Intuition over Syntax: You aren't worrying about a missing semicolon or a specific library's boilerplate. You're focused on the user experience and the system architecture.

Message:
🚀 Microsoft Fabric IQ is changing how we think about data.
Most analytics projects fail not because of data scarcity, but because definitions are misaligned. “Customer,” “order,” “active” — everyone interprets them differently. Fabric IQ flips this: start with the business meaning first, then connect the data.
It uses an ontology-first approach — a shared vocabulary that ensures consistency across dashboards, AI agents, and workflows. The result? Data that doesn’t just report, but actually understands context.
How I see this as a founder: AI and automation can only be as smart as the definitions it reasons from. Misaligned semantics lead to errors, mistrust, and wasted effort. Fabric IQ is the kind of framework that allows teams to move from descriptive analytics to intelligent action.
💡 Takeaways:
Define business meaning before building metrics.
Treat ontologies as living, governed assets.
Use shared semantics to power AI tools, dashboards, and insights.
If your organization struggles with inconsistent metrics or AI hallucinations, this is a shift worth paying attention to.
Follow for more insights on building AI-first systems and intelligent data strategies.

Message:
What is the Microsoft MVP program?
The MVP (Most Valuable Professional) award is given to individuals who:
 Actively contribute to tech communities 
 Share expertise through blogs, talks, forums, GitHub, etc. 
 Help others learn Microsoft technologies 
It’s not a certification or exam—it’s an award based on contribution and influence.
Microsoft Foundry (AI Foundry)
Azure AI Foundry (often just called “Microsoft Foundry”) is a platform from Microsoft designed to help organizations build, deploy, and manage AI applications and agents at scale.
🔧 What it actually does
Think of it as a control center for AI development:
 Build AI apps using multiple models (OpenAI, open-source, etc.) 
 Manage prompts, datasets, and evaluations 
 Deploy AI agents into production 
 Monitor performance, safety, and cost.
 MCP Servers (Model Context Protocol)
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an emerging standard that allows AI models (like Copilot or LLMs) to securely interact with external tools, APIs, and data sources.
💡 Simple way to understand MCP
 MCP = “USB-C for AI tools” 
 MCP Server = a system that exposes capabilities/data to AI agents in a structured, safe way.

Message:
Microsoft Learn
Most organizations don’t have a technology problem.
They have a translation problem.
Technical teams often report vulnerabilities, incidents, and control gaps.

Executives are listening for revenue exposure, operational disruption, regulatory impact, and customer trust.
Same issue. Different language.

The leaders who rise fastest are the ones who can turn:
“Critical security flaw” → “Potential downtime during peak sales”
“Legacy architecture risk” → “Higher cost to scale and slower market response”
“Access control weakness” → “Brand trust and compliance exposure”
When technical risk gets framed as business impact, budgets move faster, decisions get clearer, and alignment becomes easier.

Risk rarely gets ignored because it’s unimportant.
It gets ignored because it was explained poorly.

Message:
AI can never replace the human experience – it can never replace “intelligence” (true intelligence). It is a tool – an extremely useful and potentially beneficial tool, if it is used correctly. 

You can construct a piece of furniture using a saw, a hammer and some nails. But to have a true work of art, you need your imagination and your experience and you need to expand your toolset to include jigs, various types of saws, various types of sanders, etc. 

AI is a tool that can help increase productivity and efficiency and gain insight into reams of data within a very short time period. But, without a human in the loop to guide the discourse and to eliminate the noise, it’s just a functional piece of furniture – it is not art. Art is precious and evokes emotion – it creates a human connection. AI cannot do that. Not truly.

For those who can adapt and learn how to use AI as a tool, rather than viewing it as something to be distrusted, they will stand a better chance of guiding something that can have a meaningful difference in society as a whole. In the right hands, AI can become art.

Tools change.
The real moat is still judgment.

from monitoring behavior to defining boundaries.

Because sustainable adoption does not come from pushing usage metrics.

even when usage scales.

But in reality, they are just another layer of abstraction.
You still have: – operating systems
– execution paths
– trust relationships
– identity boundaries
And all of them can still be exploited if they are not structurally constrained.

they do not solve the core problem.
They simply move it.
Because security is not defined by where your system runs.
It is defined by what your architecture allows.
And without enforced control models, every additional layer — including VMs — adds complexity, not resilience.
That’s where the real discussion should begin.

Message: Logging every action from day one is the operational discipline that separates production agents from demo agents. The reason most AI agent projects break in month two is that the team only logged errors, so when behaviour drifts subtly they have no trace of what changed. Full-action logging means every decision the agent made, every data source it pulled, every escalation it triggered, every approval gate it hit. We run that pattern at Fortuna for autonomous ecommerce customer service — full traceability on every ticket the agent touches, including the ones it resolved cleanly. Reliability over time is built on the actions you logged when nothing was going wrong.

I strongly agree that this is a clean breakdown. But it quietly assumes something that often isn’t there.
AI literacy.
You can assemble reasoning, tools, retrieval, orchestration and still end up with a system no one truly understands or can reliably judge.
Because the missing layer isn’t technical. It’s human.
Who decides what “the right info” is?
Who recognizes when reasoning is flawed?
Who knows when not to trust the output?
Without that, evaluation becomes guesswork and orchestration just scales confusion faster.
An AI agent isn’t just a system design problem.
It’s a literacy problem hiding in plain sight.

The harder question is:
how do you stop a fluent model from introducing structurally weak claims into a workflow that still looks clean on the surface?

- separate confidence from coherence
- retry when recovery is plausible
- escalate when the structure is unsafe

The future research workflow is not model-only.
It is model + runtime verification.

Message:
Great perspective on adoption patterns — visibility into usage is clearly important.
But adoption alone is not the real challenge.
Because increasing AI usage without redefining the underlying architecture
does not create value — it scales uncertainty.
The moment AI becomes embedded into workflows,
it is no longer just a productivity tool.
It becomes an execution layer.
And execution without enforced boundaries introduces risks
that no usage analytics can fully capture.
Low adoption may not always be a problem.
In some cases, it is a signal.
A signal that users do not fully trust the system.
Or that the system is not yet aligned with controlled execution principles.
Because the real question is not:
“How do we get people to use AI more?”
But:
“What is the system structurally allowed to do when they do?”

Message:
AI can never replace the human experience – it can never replace “intelligence” (true intelligence). It is a tool – an extremely useful and potentially beneficial tool, if it is used correctly. 

You can construct a piece of furniture using a saw, a hammer and some nails. But to have a true work of art, you need your imagination and your experience and you need to expand your toolset to include jigs, various types of saws, various types of sanders, etc. 

AI is a tool that can help increase productivity and efficiency and gain insight into reams of data within a very short time period. But, without a human in the loop to guide the discourse and to eliminate the noise, it’s just a functional piece of furniture – it is not art. Art is precious and evokes emotion – it creates a human connection. AI cannot do that. Not truly.

For those who can adapt and learn how to use AI as a tool, rather than viewing it as something to be distrusted, they will stand a better chance of guiding something that can have a meaningful difference in society as a whole. In the right hands, AI can become art.

 Build AI apps using multiple models (OpenAI, open-source, etc.)

Define business meaning before building metrics.
Treat ontologies as living, governed assets.
Use shared semantics to power AI tools, dashboards, and insights.
If your organization struggles with inconsistent metrics or AI hallucinations, this is a shift worth paying attention to.

    -  Define Constraints: You can't just say "make it good." You have to   specify the how, the why, and the for whom.
Chain of Thought: By asking the AI to "think step-by-step," you're actually auditing your own logic.
Modularize: Good prompting breaks a monolithic problem into bite-sized, solvable sub-tasks.
-    Vibe Coding: The "Flow State"
"Vibe coding" (a term popularized recently in the dev community) represents the transition from manual syntax wrestling to high-level system orchestration.
Intuition over Syntax: You aren't worrying about a missing semicolon or a specific library's boilerplate. You're focused on the user experience and the system architecture.

Message:
This is something almost every developer struggles with at the beginning — not lack of resources, but too many directions.

The real challenge isn’t learning to code… it’s learning what to ignore.

What I’ve seen (and experienced) is that most people try to consume everything — courses, frameworks, tools — but never spend enough time actually building. And that’s where the real learning happens.

Clarity comes from action, not endless planning.

A simple shift that works:

Pick one stack

Build small, real projects

Break things, fix them, repeat


That feedback loop compounds faster than any “perfect roadmap.”

In today’s AI-driven world, the game is evolving — developers who combine fundamentals with AI tools will move 10x faster. But the foundation still matters.

You don’t need the perfect path.
You need consistent progress.

Message:
Shared files get disorganized so quickly because Microsoft didn’t think through this sharing process at all or they figured they could reinvent the wheel but stopped before completing the full idea. Primarily, the side of the user being shared with. If someone shares a file with me, it shows up in my Shared section of OneDrive. If 100 people share 200 files with me over whatever amount of time, I have a long list in Shared that I can’t structure in any way. I have to use the search and I’m at the mercy of this list. Unlike many other competitor products storing and sharing files, Microsoft doesn’t let me move these shared files to my own document structure to store it where it actually makes sense. I can create a Shortcut from my folders to it, but if the other end stops sharing with me now I have a shortcut that goes nowhere that I am responsible for cleaning up.

I truly wish Microsoft would have fully thought things out before releasing a half baked product that they figured they would just update and patch along the way because what they consider a priority to patch and update doesn’t line up with the real world users, the workflows they use, and the problems they face.

We run a course on Microsoft 365 and the amount of things we have to explain workarounds for is something else. Many, many businesses are using these products and despite the money they pay for it, some very basic functionality that is at the core of what Microsoft offers still doesn’t work as most people would expect it to. 🤷‍♂️
